trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day technical trip: ~4.5-hr approach to a base bivy, then a ~12.5-hr day for 9 pitches of 5.10 and the walk-off descent.

days.title: Approach to base camp
days.objective: Reach the base of the Southwest Face and bivy
days.note: Same approach as the other SW Face lines: Bedal Creek Trail 2.5 miles to the washout, then up the basin to the base of the wall. Bivy at the base.

days.title: Climb Diamond in the Rough and descend
days.objective: Climb the 9-pitch 5.10 line to the upper mountain, then descend to the car
days.note: Climb roughly 1,100 ft over 9 pitches of 5.10 rock (Grade III) up the SW Face, finishing into 3rd-class terrain near the summit. Descend via the neighboring Corkscrew line back to the trail.

camps_on_file.name: Bedal Campground, Mountain Loop Highway
camps_on_file.notes: The closest road camp to the Sloan Peak and Bedal Creek trailheads, and the standard place to sleep the night before a Sloan attempt since the useful start time is well before dawn. It sits on the unpaved stretch of the loop, so access depends entirely on whether the seasonal gate between Barlow Pass and the Bedal area…

camps_on_file.name: Bivy at the base of Sloan's southwest face
camps_on_file.notes: Reached from the Bedal Creek trailhead by the west-face approach, traversing over a notch to the southwest. Parties who do not climb in a single long day sleep here.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day technical outing: ~4.5 hrs approach to a base bivy, then a long ~13-hr summit day with 8 pitches of 5.10d and a multi-stage Corkscrew descent.

days.title: Approach to base camp
days.objective: Reach the base of the Southwest Face and bivy
days.note: Hike the Bedal Creek Trail 2.5 miles to the washout, then scramble/bushwhack up the basin and traverse around a notch to the SW Face. Bivy at the base near running water.

days.title: Climb Fire on the Mountain and descend
days.objective: Send the 8-pitch 5.10d line, tag the summit, and descend to the car
days.note: Climb roughly 1,000 ft of sustained 5.10 rock over 8 pitches, then 500 ft of 3rd-class scrambling to the summit. Descend the Corkscrew line: downclimb from the gear stash, drop a heathered gully, follow the access ramp, then downclimb slabs and traverse back around the mountain to the trail.

camps_on_file.name: Bedal Campground, Mountain Loop Highway
camps_on_file.notes: The closest road camp to the Sloan Peak and Bedal Creek trailheads, and the standard place to sleep the night before a Sloan attempt since the useful start time is well before dawn. It sits on the unpaved stretch of the loop, so access depends entirely on whether the seasonal gate between Barlow Pass and the Bedal area…

camps_on_file.name: Bivy at the base of Sloan's southwest face
camps_on_file.notes: Reached from the Bedal Creek trailhead by the west-face approach, traversing over a notch to the southwest. Parties who do not climb in a single long day sleep here.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day trip: ~4.5-hr approach to a base bivy, then a long ~15-hr climbing day covering 9 pitches, a summit scramble, and the full Corkscrew walk-off.

days.title: Approach to base camp
days.objective: Reach the base of the Northwest Buttress and bivy
days.note: Same Bedal Basin approach as the West Face routes: hike up through the meadows below the broad west face to the corner of darker rock at the low left side of the buttress. Bivy at the base.

days.title: Climb the Northwest Buttress and descend
days.objective: Climb 9 pitches to the upper mountain, tag the summit, and descend to the car
days.note: Climb 9 pitches (about 1,800 ft, Grade IV 5.9+) up the buttress, exiting via a short hand crack onto the upper mountain, then 3rd/4th-class scrambling to the sub-summit and main summit, joining the upper Corkscrew line for the descent.

camps_on_file.name: Bedal Campground, Mountain Loop Highway
camps_on_file.notes: The closest road camp to the Sloan Peak and Bedal Creek trailheads, and the standard place to sleep the night before a Sloan attempt since the useful start time is well before dawn. It sits on the unpaved stretch of the loop, so access depends entirely on whether the seasonal gate between Barlow Pass and the Bedal area…

camps_on_file.name: Bivy at the base of Sloan's southwest face
camps_on_file.notes: On the Bedal Creek approach below the west and southwest faces. Parties who do not climb in a single long day sleep near the base of the face.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day version for parties who prefer a high camp near the glacier toe: ~4.5 hrs in, then an ~11-hr summit-and-walk-out day.

days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach camp at the saddle / glacier toe
days.note: Hike the Bedal Creek Trail and climbers' path up into the basin. Camp on the saddle (~5,300 ft) or the ridge overlooking the glacier (~5,800 ft) — expect to camp on snow into June.

days.title: Summit push and hike out
days.objective: Climb to the summit via the Corkscrew, then break camp and hike all the way out
days.note: From camp, cross the lower glacier and climb the Corkscrew's sloping shelf through the cliff band to the summit, then reverse the route back to camp, break it down, and hike out to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Ridge above the Sloan Glacier
camps_on_file.notes: The preferred high camp, on the crest overlooking the glacier with a long view. From here it is about half a mile of traverse east-southeast to the saddle near 5,900 ft and then up to gain the glacier around 6,800 ft, which makes for a short summit morning. Expect to camp on snow through June; the route's window is squ…

camps_on_file.name: Bedal-Sloan saddle
camps_on_file.notes: The first camp on the ridge, reached by traversing open and partly brushy slopes past a small lake. Usable, but the ridge above is the better camp and most parties who carry a camp go the extra distance. Elevation is given as either 5,330 or 5,380 ft depending on the account.

camps_on_file.name: Bedal Creek roadhead
camps_on_file.notes: Worth recording because it is the overnight most Sloan parties actually use. The Corkscrew from Bedal Creek is a reasonable single day of thirteen or fourteen hours for a fit party, and successful ascents in under twelve hours are common, so the usual pattern is to sleep at the trailhead and start around four in the mo…

trip_plan.totalNote: Backpack the North Fork Sauk Trail to a camp near White Pass or Indian Pass, then climb Indian Head Peak and hike out.

days.title: Hike to White Pass or Indian Pass
days.objective: Camp near White Pass or Indian Pass
days.note: Hike the North Fork Sauk Trail from the trailhead to a camp near White Pass or Indian Pass, roughly 10 miles to White Pass or 13-14 miles to Indian Pass with about 4,000+ ft of gain.

days.title: Climb Indian Head Peak and hike out
days.objective: Scramble the summit from camp and return
days.note: Climb Indian Head Peak round trip from camp, an off-trail scramble of several hours. Then either hike out or camp again and hike out on an optional Day 3.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day, ~28-30 mile round trip with roughly 6,150 ft of gain: one long approach day to a ~6,700 ft glacier-basin camp, an alpine-start summit day (9-10 hrs round trip) crossing the White Chuck and White River Glaciers, and a hike back out.

days.title: Approach to White Chuck Glacier basin camp
days.objective: Reach high camp (~6,700 ft) in the White Chuck River basin near Foam Pass
days.note: From the North Fork Sauk River Trailhead (2,050 ft), follow the North Fork Sauk Trail past Red Creek and the old Mackinaw Shelter site, then climb steeply (about 3,000 ft in 4 miles) to White Pass (5,900 ft). Continue over Foam Pass and drop into the White Chuck River basin, camping near Lake 6433 at roughly 6,700 ft. …

days.title: Summit push via White Chuck & White River Glaciers
days.objective: Climb Kololo Peaks' true (east) summit, 8,240 ft
days.note: Alpine start to cross the White Chuck Glacier with crampons, over Glacier Gap onto the White River Glacier, then scramble talus/ledges to the west summit before a short traverse to the higher east summit. Round trip from camp typically runs 9-10 hours.

days.title: Hike out to trailhead
days.objective: Return to North Fork Sauk River Trailhead
days.note: Reverse Day 1: back over Foam Pass and White Pass, then down the North Fork Sauk Trail to the car. Fast parties have reported under 5 hours; a more typical pace with full packs is 6+ hours.

camps_on_file.name: White Chuck Glacier basin, under Kololo Peaks
camps_on_file.notes: The climbing camp for Kololo Peaks, and the reason Kololo is a three-day trip rather than a weekend scramble. It sits in the stark rock-and-snow basin on the edge of what remains of the White Chuck Glacier, reached from the North Fork Sauk road end by twelve or thirteen miles of walking — the long river approach, then …

camps_on_file.name: Sloan Creek Campground and the North Fork Sauk road end
camps_on_file.notes: The staging point for the eastern half of this zone and the drive-in night before two very different trips. Painted mountain, which older maps and signs call Red Mountain, goes from right here as a day objective with no established camp anywhere on it: a mile of maintained trail to about 3,100 ft, then a short steep st…

trip_plan.totalNote: Cross Cascade Pass, Cache Col and the Middle Cascade Glacier to Yang Yang Lakes, climb Le Conte from camp, and reverse the approach.

days.title: Cascade Pass to Yang Yang Lakes
days.objective: Camp at Yang Yang Lakes
days.note: Hike from the Cascade Pass Trailhead to Cascade Pass and over Cache Col and the Cache Glacier, descend to Kool-Aid Lake, and cross the Middle Cascade Glacier to the Yang Yang Lakes camp. It is a long day of about 13 miles with 9,000+ ft of cumulative gain.

days.title: Climb Le Conte Mountain
days.objective: Summit via the east-slope ledge route
days.note: Climb Le Conte Mountain round trip from camp via the east-slope and ledge route.

days.title: Reverse the approach to the trailhead
days.objective: Return over Cache Col to Cascade Pass
days.note: Reverse the approach back to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Le Conte Pass
camps_on_file.notes: The pass sits on the shoulder above the lakes in the basin below Le Conte Mountain, and it is the direct base for Le Conte itself, which is climbed by working up its east slope on talus and blocky rock by the line of least resistance rather than by any single defined route. It is also where parties running late stop in…

camps_on_file.name: Yang Yang Lakes
camps_on_file.notes: Reached by crossing Spider-Formidable Col and descending snow and scree. The standard camp for Le Conte, which is climbed from here in a day.

camps_on_file.name: Cache Col and the Cache Glacier shoulder
camps_on_file.notes: The col is the gateway to everything here. From the Cascade Pass trail a boot path climbs south along the arm and onto the mellow Cache Glacier, which is corniced at the col early in the season and can need a careful step through. Parties who leave the car in the afternoon and lose the light on the climb sometimes stop…

camps_on_file.name: Spider-Formidable Col
camps_on_file.notes: The working base camp for both Spider Mountain and Mount Formidable, and the reason to know about it is that a party climbing either peak stops here while a party walking the traverse does not. The twin notches of the col divide the two mountains, and it is reached by crossing the upper Middle Cascade Glacier almost du…

trip_plan.totalNote: A 7-day, ~35 mi out-and-back from Cascade Pass with ~11,200 ft of cumulative gain and about the same loss; Lizard Mountain itself is a ~3 mi, 3-4 hr round-trip Class 2-3 scramble on a layover day from the White Rock Lakes camp, usually day 4.

days.title: Cascade Pass to Kool-Aid Lake
days.objective: Reach Kool-Aid Lake camp
days.note: Standard maintained trail up to Cascade Pass, then off-trail up and over Cache Col into the Kool-Aid Lake basin below Cache Glacier. This is the last easy trail walking of the trip -- everything after is off-trail alpine travel.

days.title: Kool-Aid Lake to Yang-Yang Lakes
days.objective: Cross Cache/Middle Cascade Glaciers to Yang-Yang Lakes
days.note: The technical crux day of the northern half: rope up for glacier travel across the Cache and Middle Cascade Glaciers, negotiate the Red Ledges / Le Conte area, then drop to camp at Yang-Yang Lakes. Crevasse hazard and route-finding make this the slowest-per-mile day of the trip.

days.title: Yang-Yang Lakes to White Rock Lakes
days.objective: Reach White Rock Lakes via Lizard Pass
days.note: A shorter day over Lizard Pass (Lizard Col, ~6,798 ft) and down into the White Rock Lakes basin, widely regarded as one of the most scenic campsites in the Cascades. Most parties treat this as a half-day with time to relax at camp.

days.title: Layover: Lizard Mountain scramble
days.objective: Scramble Lizard Mountain (South Route) from camp
days.note: A dedicated layover day at White Rock Lakes with a half-day round-trip scramble to the Lizard Mountain summit: regain Lizard Pass, climb the loose south ridge to the 7,420 ft summit, then descend the west ridge back to the pass. The scramble is straightforward but somewhat loose Class 2. Carry only a light day pack -- …

days.title: White Rock Lakes to Yang-Yang Lakes
days.objective: Start back north over Lizard Col to Yang-Yang Lakes
days.note: Begin the return the way you came: climb to Lizard Col, cross the South Cascade Glacier and work around Sentinel Peak on the Le Conte Glacier, then descend to camp at Yang-Yang Lakes. Rope up for both glaciers.

days.title: Yang-Yang Lakes to Kool-Aid Lake
days.objective: Recross the Middle Cascade Glacier and the Red Ledge to Kool-Aid Lake
days.note: Climb to the gap beside Spider Mountain and make the roped crossing of the Middle Cascade Glacier, then traverse the Red Ledge and descend to Kool-Aid Lake. The glacier and the ledge are the day's route-finding and crevasse concerns, as on the way in.

days.title: Kool-Aid Lake to Cascade Pass Trailhead
days.objective: Over Cache Col and down to the car
days.note: Climb to Cache Col, descend the Cache Glacier and traverse back across the Mixup flank to Cascade Pass, then follow the maintained trail down to the Cascade River Road. Mostly downhill, and no shuttle is needed because the trip ends where it began.

camps_on_file.name: Sentinel Pass and Lizard Col
camps_on_file.notes: The two saddles either side of Sentinel Peak, crossed one after the other on the way from the Le Conte Glacier to the South Cascade Glacier. These are the highest useful sleeping spots on this part of the crest and the direct bases for Sentinel Peak and for Lizard Mountain, which stands just east of the col that carrie…

camps_on_file.name: Crest bivouacs above the South Cascade and Chickamin glaciers
camps_on_file.notes: Say it plainly: these are not sites, they are wherever a party gets to. Elephant Head is the southernmost peak, standing on the divide above the lakes at the south end of the crest with big cliffs dropping east into the head of the west fork of Agnes Creek, between the ice on either side. It gets a handful of ascents i…

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day, ~21-mile round trip with roughly 4,900-5,000 ft of total gain: an easy approach day into Twin Lakes camp followed by a long (9-10 hr) summit day that finishes by hiking and biking all the way back to the car.

days.title: Bike & hike to Twin Lakes camp
days.objective: Reach the Twin Lakes basin and set up camp
days.note: From Barlow Pass, most parties mountain-bike the gated Monte Cristo road to save time, then hike Forest Trail #708 over Poodle Dog Pass to Twin Lakes. It's a mellow, scenic approach day with time to swim or fish once camp is set.

days.title: Summit via West Spur, hike all the way out
days.objective: Climb Columbia Peak and return to the trailhead same day
days.note: Leave camp with a light day pack, stash overnight gear partway up, and climb the West Spur past loose ledges and a short snow patch to a single 4th-class crux move that gains the southwest face. After the summit, retrace the full route back to camp, out to Poodle Dog Pass, and bike the old wagon road to the car — a lon…

camps_on_file.name: Twin Lakes basin, under the west face of Columbia
camps_on_file.notes: The high camp for the southern half of the group. Columbia Peak's west spur rises straight off this basin and is the reason most parties come, and the Columbia Glacier route on Kyes is staged from here too, working up the glacier pinched between Columbia and Kyes to the weakness high on it. Reaching the lakes is the ha…

camps_on_file.name: Monte Cristo townsite campground, four miles up the closed road
camps_on_file.notes: Because the road is gated at Barlow Pass, staging here is the normal plan for this group rather than a luxury: it turns a four-mile approach walk into an evening stroll and puts Glacier Basin, Poodle Dog Pass and every summit above them within a sane day. The walk in follows the old road and railway grade with almost n…

camps_on_file.name: Barlow Pass roadhead
camps_on_file.notes: Sleeping at the car is what most parties actually do the night before a long single push into this group, because the four-mile road walk to the townsite is flat and fast enough to be swallowed by a pre-dawn start. It is the last point vehicles reach: the gate closes the Monte Cristo road here, and it is also where the…

camps_on_file.name: Silver Lake, below Poodle Dog Pass
camps_on_file.notes: A short side trail from Poodle Dog Pass drops to the lake, which makes it the softer option on this side of the group: it is a good thousand feet lower than Twin Lakes and it avoids the steep, loose drop into and back out of that basin at the end of a summit day. Parties heading for Columbia often sleep here instead an…

campsite_pins.name: Monte Cristo townsite campground, four miles up the closed road

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day, ~16-mile round trip with about 4,800 ft total gain — the standard way organized/club parties do this climb given the technical col, moat crossing, and washed-out approach road, though strong/fast parties do climb it car-to-car in a single long (10-14 hr) day using bikes for the approach.

days.title: Bike & backpack in to Glacier Basin camp
days.objective: Reach high camp in upper Glacier Basin
days.note: From Barlow Pass (2,360 ft) bike or hike the washed-out mining road 4.2 miles to the Monte Cristo townsite, then follow the Glacier Basin trail 2.5 miles past Glacier Falls and behind Mystery Hill to camp in upper Glacier Basin (~4,500 ft). Bikes cut the flat road section to well under an hour and are what most current…

days.title: North Col route to the summit, then out to the car
days.objective: Climb the North Col route and descend all the way to Barlow Pass
days.note: An alpine-start day: talus and steep snow (to ~45°) lead up the center gully to the North Col, then a short traverse, moat crossing, and ~75 ft summit gully (a few mid-5th-class moves, rope/belay commonly used) gain the summit ridge. Descent reverses the route — downclimbing or rappelling the short chimney — before bre…

camps_on_file.name: Glacier Basin — Ray's Knoll and Mystery Hill
camps_on_file.notes: This is the working high camp for the northern half of the group. Cadet forms the basin's north arc and Monte Cristo Peak the southeast arc, so both go as reasonable summit days from here rather than the brutal round trips they are from the road. Foggy Peak rises straight out of the ground immediately northeast of the …

It is the last point vehicles reach: the gate closes the Monte Cristo road here, and it is also where the…

trip_plan.totalNote: An overnight trip: walk or bike to Monte Cristo and camp in Glacier Basin, then climb East Wilmans Spire the next morning and return to Barlow Pass the same day.

days.title: Hike in to Glacier Basin
days.objective: Camp at Glacier Basin
days.note: Travel from Barlow Pass to Monte Cristo and up the Glacier Basin Trail to camp in Glacier Basin.

days.title: Climb East Wilmans Spire and exit
days.objective: Climb the spire and return to Barlow Pass
days.note: Climb East Wilmans Spire in the morning. Then hike and bike back out to Barlow Pass the same day.

camps_on_file.name: Glacier Basin — Ray's Knoll and Mystery Hill
camps_on_file.notes: This is the working high camp for the northern half of the group. Cadet forms the basin's north arc and Monte Cristo Peak the southeast arc, so both go as reasonable summit days from here rather than the brutal round trips they are from the road. Foggy Peak rises straight out of the ground immediately northeast of the …

camps_on_file.notes: Because the road is gated at Barlow Pass, staging here is the normal plan for this group rather than a luxury: it turns a four-mile approach walk into an evening stroll and puts Glacier Basin, Poodle Dog Pass and every summit above them within a sane day. The walk in follows the old road and railway grade with almost n…

camps_on_file.notes: Sleeping at the car is what most parties actually do the night before a long single push into this group, because the four-mile road walk to the townsite is flat and fast enough to be swallowed by a pre-dawn start. It is the last point vehicles reach: the gate closes the Monte Cristo road here, and it is also where the…

campsite_pins.name: Monte Cristo townsite campground, four miles up the closed road

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day backpack is the common approach for this remote, seldom-climbed peak: ~6 mi/3,400 ft in to a camp at Airplane Lake, then a summit push plus full hike-out (~9 mi, ~5,400 ft of net loss) the next day; very fit parties have also pushed the whole ~15-16 mi, ~5,300 ft round trip car-to-car in a single long day (documented at 7.3 hr up / 4.4 hr down).

days.title: Approach to Airplane Lake camp
days.objective: Reach Airplane Lake and set up camp
days.note: From the White River trailhead, follow the flat Indian Creek Trail for 4.5 easy miles, then turn off onto a steep, brushy climber's path that gains 2,200 ft in 1.5 miles through old burn and vine maple to reach Airplane Lake. Camp on the lake's north-side peninsula, a known flat, bug-free spot used by most parties.

days.title: Summit push and hike out
days.objective: Climb Mount Saul via the East Slopes and hike back to the trailhead
days.note: From camp, boulder-hop the lake's outlet and beeline toward the low point on the ridge east of the summit, then follow the ridge crest through a short rock band to the broad summit (register sits ~15 ft below and west of the high point). Early-season parties often kick steps up a continuous snowfield above ~4,700 ft. A…

camps_on_file.name: Airplane Lake
camps_on_file.notes: This is the camp for Mount Saul and effectively the only one, and camping here is what turns a brutal outing into a reasonable two days. Done in a single push from the road the standard route runs about sixteen miles round trip with five thousand three hundred feet of gain, which is a long day by any measure and a very…

camps_on_file.name: White River road end trailhead
camps_on_file.notes: The staging point for the whole trip, and worth its own entry because the drive is where this approach most often fails. The White River road leaves the Lake Wenatchee end and turns to gravel several miles before the trailhead, ending at about 2,300 feet where the White River trail, the Indian Creek trail, the Mount Da…

camps_on_file.name: The Indian Creek valley camps and the Airplane Lake junction site
camps_on_file.notes: The junction camp is the useful one and it is the landmark as much as the site: the climbers' path for Airplane Lake turns off immediately before it, so a party that reaches an obvious valley campsite and has seen no turning has just walked past the only one there is. Sleeping here rather than at the lake trades a shor…

camps_on_file.name: The east slope above Airplane Lake — no established camp
camps_on_file.notes: The honest answer for this peak is that Airplane Lake is the camp and there is nothing above it worth having. The lake already puts the summit within a straightforward morning on the east slope and east face, so climbing higher with a pack buys almost nothing and costs the water, the shelter and the flat ground all at …

trip_plan.totalNote: A six-day north-to-south Ptarmigan Traverse with a climbing day from White Rock Lakes for Old Guard's east ridge, exiting by Itswoot Ridge and Downey Creek.

days.title: Cascade Pass to Kool-Aid Lake
days.objective: Cross Cache Col to the first camp
days.note: Switchback 3.7 mi up to Cascade Pass, head south up the Mix-up Arm, cross the Cache Glacier to Cache Col, then drop southwest to Kool-Aid Lake. Cache Col has no water, so some parties camp there and carry it up.

days.title: Red Ledge and Middle Cascade to Yang Yang
days.objective: Reach Yang Yang Lakes
days.note: Traverse past the Red Ledge, cross the Middle Cascade Glacier above the icefall to the Spider-Formidable col, then descend steep snow (up to 40 degrees or more) and granite benches under Formidable to the lakes.

days.title: Le Conte Glacier to White Rock Lakes
days.objective: Reach White Rock Lakes
days.note: Go via Le Conte Pass and up the Le Conte Glacier to the Sentinel-Le Conte saddle, then down onto the South Cascade Glacier and over Lizard Pass to the lakes.

days.title: Climb Old Guard Peak's east ridge
days.objective: Summit Old Guard and return to White Rock Lakes
days.note: Go back up onto the Le Conte Glacier and climb Old Guard's east ridge: two pitches of mid-fifth class to the summit. Sentinel's SW ridge is often climbed the same day. Old Guard can also be reached from the Old Guard-Sentinel col by a third-class scramble.

days.title: Dana Glacier to Itswoot Ridge
days.objective: Cross to the Itswoot Ridge or Cub Lake camp
days.note: Drop toward the West Fork Agnes, climb a snow and scree gully onto the Dana Glacier and over a 7,600 ft col with a short Class 3 step, then descend and traverse three gullies to camp on Itswoot Ridge near 6,400 ft. Cub Lake is about an hour farther.

days.title: Bachelor Creek and Downey Creek out
days.objective: Walk out to the Downey Creek trailhead
days.note: Over the 6,000 ft saddle into Bachelor Creek (2-3 h), down the brushy creek with a crossing near 3,750 ft to Six Mile camp on Downey Creek (3-5 h), then 6.6 mi of maintained trail.

camps_on_file.name: Yang Yang Lakes
camps_on_file.notes: The second camp for most north-to-south parties, sitting in a shallow bowl below Le Conte Mountain after the drop off the Middle Cascade Glacier. It is the natural base for Old Guard Peak, whose summit is reached from the Le Conte Glacier above by a class 2 to 3 snow couloir and short scramble on the west side, or by t…

camps_on_file.name: White Rock Lakes
camps_on_file.notes: The third camp and the one most parties remember, reached from Yang Yang across the Le Conte Glacier and the Le Conte-Sentinel col, then down a long traverse under Sentinel and Old Guard. It looks straight across at Dome Peak and the Dana Glacier, which is the day that follows. Sinister Peak is not climbed from here di…

camps_on_file.name: Kool-Aid Lake
camps_on_file.notes: The first camp on the traverse coming from Cascade Pass, reached by climbing to Cache Col and dropping a short but awkward distance southwest to the tarn. It is where the permit regime changes, which is the practical reason to know it exists even if you are only passing through. Published elevations vary by a couple of…

trip_plan.totalNote: A 6-day, roughly 33-mile glacier traverse (Cascade Pass to the Suiattle River) with on the order of 11,000-12,000 ft of cumulative gain; Old Guard Peak itself is a ~2.5-3 hr round-trip snow-couloir-and-scramble side summit from Sentinel Pass on day 3, not a stand-alone car-to-car objective.

days.title: Approach to Kool-Aid Lake via Cache Col
days.objective: Reach high camp below Cache Col
days.note: From the Cascade Pass trailhead, hike the maintained trail to Cascade Pass, then climb switchbacks to Cache Col (~6,900 ft) before dropping to a camp near Kool-Aid Lake / upper Basin Creek. This is the last on-trail day; everything after is off-trail glacier and ridge travel.

days.title: Glacier travel to Yang Yang Lakes
days.objective: Cross to Yang Yang Lakes via Red Ledge and Spider-Formidable Col
days.note: Rope up for the Cascade/Middle Cascade Glacier crossing, traverse the exposed Red Ledge, and cross Spider-Formidable Col before dropping to camp at Yang Yang Lakes. Slow going relative to the mileage due to glacier travel and route-finding.

days.title: Sentinel Pass and the Old Guard Peak summit
days.objective: Summit Old Guard Peak via the northwest snow couloir and Class 3 scramble
days.note: The long day of the trip: cross the LeConte Glacier to Sentinel Pass, drop packs, and knock off Old Guard Peak via a steep snowfinger and short Class 3 gabbro scramble on its west/northwest side. Continue on to camp at White Rock Lakes; many parties also tag LeConte Mountain from the same pass.

days.title: Traverse toward the Dome Peak area
days.objective: Continue south to Itswoot Ridge / Dana-Dome Saddle
days.note: Cross South Cascade and Dana Glacier terrain toward Itswoot Ridge, camping near the Dana-Dome Saddle. Many parties use this camp for an optional Dome Peak side summit, though it isn't required for the Old Guard objective.

days.title: Descend toward Bachelor Meadow
days.objective: Drop off the high traverse into the Bachelor Creek drainage
days.note: A shorter day easing down off the glaciated high country toward timberline camp at Bachelor Meadow, staging for the long exit hike.

days.title: Exit via Bachelor and Downey Creek
days.objective: Hike out to the Suiattle River Road trailhead
days.note: A long, brushy exit down the climbers'-path-quality Bachelor Creek trail to Downey Creek and the Suiattle River Road. Expect log crossings and overgrown tread low down; most parties pre-arrange a car shuttle since this is a different trailhead than the Cascade Pass start.

camps_on_file.name: Yang Yang Lakes
camps_on_file.notes: The second camp for most north-to-south parties, sitting in a shallow bowl below Le Conte Mountain after the drop off the Middle Cascade Glacier. It is the natural base for Old Guard Peak, whose summit is reached from the Le Conte Glacier above by a class 2 to 3 snow couloir and short scramble on the west side, or by t…

camps_on_file.name: Kool-Aid Lake
camps_on_file.notes: The first camp on the traverse coming from Cascade Pass, reached by climbing to Cache Col and dropping a short but awkward distance southwest to the tarn. It is where the permit regime changes, which is the practical reason to know it exists even if you are only passing through. Published elevations vary by a couple of…

camps_on_file.name: White Rock Lakes
camps_on_file.notes: The third camp and the one most parties remember, reached from Yang Yang across the Le Conte Glacier and the Le Conte-Sentinel col, then down a long traverse under Sentinel and Old Guard. It looks straight across at Dome Peak and the Dana Glacier, which is the day that follows. Sinister Peak is not climbed from here di…

trip_plan.totalNote: Three days on the Ptarmigan Traverse reach the col between Le Conte and Sentinel, where the line onto Rimrock Ridge begins. No published account gives a schedule for the ridge itself or for leaving it, so no total length is stated here.

days.title: Cascade Pass trailhead to Kool-Aid Lake
days.objective: Reach Kool-Aid Lake, the usual first camp on the traverse
days.note: Climb the Cascade Pass trail, then follow the traverse's climbers' path up and over Cache Col and down to camp at Kool-Aid Lake.

days.title: Kool-Aid Lake to Yang Yang Lakes
days.objective: Reach Yang Yang Lakes, the usual second camp
days.note: Cross the exposed Red Ledge below Arts Knoll, rope up for the Middle Cascade Glacier, pass through the Spider–Formidable col and descend to camp at Yang Yang Lakes.

days.title: Yang Yang Lakes to the Le Conte–Sentinel col
days.objective: Leave the traverse for the west end of Rimrock Ridge
days.note: Climb back to the Le Conte ridge and up the Le Conte Glacier toward the col at its head beside Sentinel Peak. Leave the traverse here, pass north of Sentinel and head east onto the ridge crest.

camps_on_file.name: Kool-Aid Lake
camps_on_file.notes: The usual first camp on the traverse, south of Cache Col.

camps_on_file.name: Yang Yang Lakes
camps_on_file.notes: The usual second camp, below the Spider–Formidable col; well-established sites by the lakes.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 4-day glacier backpack, roughly 34 miles and 8,500 ft cumulative gain round trip, with high camps at Cache Col/Kool-Aid Lakes and Le Conte-Sentinel Col; strong parties compress this to 3 days by pushing all the way to the col on day 1.

days.title: Approach to Cache Col / Kool-Aid Lakes
days.objective: Cross Cascade Pass and Cache Col, establish first camp
days.note: From the Cascade River Road trailhead (add 2+ miles of road walking if the seasonal washout below the trailhead hasn't been repaired), climb through forest and meadow to Cascade Pass, then continue up over Cache Col into the basin near Kool-Aid Lakes. This is the heaviest pack day of the trip with a full load of camp a…

days.title: Glacier traverse to high camp at Le Conte-Sentinel Col
days.objective: Reach Le Conte-Sentinel Col (7,300 ft) high camp
days.note: Rope up for glacier travel: cross the Red Ledges, the Middle Cascade Glacier, and the Spider-Formidable col, then drop to Yang Yang Lakes before climbing to a high camp at Le Conte-Sentinel Col, directly below Sentinel Peak's west face. This is the technical crux of getting into position and typically the longest day o…

days.title: Summit Sentinel + Old Guard, move camp down
days.objective: Climb Sentinel Peak (8,257 ft) and Old Guard Peak, descend to Yang Yang Lakes
days.note: Drop packs and climb Sentinel's west face: ascend a steepening snow ramp to about 7,400 ft, take a ledge system left/north past cliff bands, then finish on low 5th-class rock steps to the west ridge and the summit. Many parties tag class-3 Old Guard Peak from the same col before descending to a lower camp at Yang Yang …

days.title: Exit to trailhead
days.objective: Hike out via Cascade Pass to the road
days.note: Retrace the route from Yang Yang Lakes back over Cascade Pass to the Cascade River Road trailhead (plus the road walk if it's still washed out). Mostly downhill but with the final climb back over the pass before the long descent to the car.

camps_on_file.name: Sentinel Pass and Lizard Col
camps_on_file.notes: The two saddles either side of Sentinel Peak, crossed one after the other on the way from the Le Conte Glacier to the South Cascade Glacier. These are the highest useful sleeping spots on this part of the crest and the direct bases for Sentinel Peak and for Lizard Mountain, which stands just east of the col that carrie…

camps_on_file.name: White Rock Lakes
camps_on_file.notes: The camp at the south end of the high traverse, under the Dana and Chickamin glaciers. Sentinel and Old Guard are climbed from here or from the col above.

camps_on_file.name: Cache Col and the Cache Glacier shoulder
camps_on_file.notes: The col is the gateway to everything here. From the Cascade Pass trail a boot path climbs south along the arm and onto the mellow Cache Glacier, which is corniced at the col early in the season and can need a careful step through. Parties who leave the car in the afternoon and lose the light on the climb sometimes stop…

camps_on_file.name: Spider-Formidable Col
camps_on_file.notes: The working base camp for both Spider Mountain and Mount Formidable, and the reason to know about it is that a party climbing either peak stops here while a party walking the traverse does not. The twin notches of the col divide the two mountains, and it is reached by crossing the upper Middle Cascade Glacier almost du…

camps_on_file.name: Le Conte Pass
camps_on_file.notes: The pass sits on the shoulder above the lakes in the basin below Le Conte Mountain, and it is the direct base for Le Conte itself, which is climbed by working up its east slope on talus and blocky rock by the line of least resistance rather than by any single defined route. It is also where parties running late stop in…

camps_on_file.name: Crest bivouacs above the South Cascade and Chickamin glaciers
camps_on_file.notes: Say it plainly: these are not sites, they are wherever a party gets to. Elephant Head is the southernmost peak, standing on the divide above the lakes at the south end of the crest with big cliffs dropping east into the head of the west fork of Agnes Creek, between the ice on either side. It gets a handful of ascents i…

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day trip: roughly 11.8 mi round trip with about 4,300 ft of cumulative gain, backpacking in to Gothic Basin then traversing past Weden Pass to Sheep Gap's main summit before hiking all the way out. Strong parties instead push the whole thing car-to-car as a single very long (10-17 hr) day.

days.title: Approach to Gothic Basin camp
days.objective: Backpack in to a camp near the Gothic Basin tarns
days.note: From Barlow Pass, walk the gated Monte Cristo road about a mile, then climb the rough, rocky Weden Creek/Gothic Basin Trail #724 through timber and steep switchbacks into subalpine terrain. Camp near the tarns below Foggy Lake to stage for the summit traverse.

days.title: Weden Pass traverse, main summit, hike out
days.objective: Climb Sheep Gap Mountain's 5,814' main summit, then hike all the way out
days.note: Traverse steep heather and talus south of camp to Weden Pass (5,120'), then traverse south-west, dropping to about 4,900 ft beneath the cliff bands, to the notch below the main summit. Lead the short class 4 step, scramble to the 5,814' summit, rappel the step and reverse the traverse to Weden Pass before descending al…

camps_on_file.name: Foggy Lake, Gothic Basin
camps_on_file.notes: From here both Del Campo and Gothic go as short snow-and-scramble outings, which is why parties carry in rather than push either from the road.
